pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/features/home/sub_welcome/lib/sinceLeftBriefing.ts:84 The since-you-left briefing counts a run whose process died (status `incomplete`, written by the zombie sweep as a distinct status) as `failed`. SinceYouLeftBriefing.tsx:41 then shows it to the operator as "N failed" in the error tone, so this projection renders an unknown outcome as a definite failure verdict.

techniques.evidence: src/features/home/sub_welcome/lib/sinceLeftBriefing.ts:84 The record keeps `incomplete` as its own status, which is good. This consumer folds it back into the failure count (via isLostRun in src/features/home/lib/lostRun.ts), so a person sees a definite failure verdict for work the record marks as unknown. Surfacing these runs on the resume pointer (useResumeContext.ts:202) is the human-decides disposition the technique asks for, but there too they are labelled as failures.

pairs.registryProposal: The technique states the indeterminate status must not be rendered as a value for the model and for machine consumers. It could say explicitly that operator-facing summaries (counts, tones) must keep it distinct from failure too: the gap seen here is a correct writer with a consumer that collapses its status.
